clue.text: Still in bed, not having been chosen

definitions.meaning: a flower not yet gathered remains growing in its flowerbed

explanation.definitionFit: Flowers left growing in the bed were never gathered, and a person passed over was likewise never selected.

clue.text: Tailless bird that is in fashion!

indicators.note: without its tail means the last letter of the bird word is dropped

parts.note: a chick is a young bird

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a bird with no tail that has become fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' removes the final K from CHICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something stylish and elegant is in fashion.

clue.text: This duck is a fish!

parts.note: the duck named after an Indian city is no bird but a small dried fish eaten in curries

explanation.definitionFit: The so-called duck of this Indian city is really a lizardfish, dried and salted as a relish.

clue.text: Understand it is gold he takes

parts.note: to understand an idea can mean to accept it
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone grasping that the metal is gold as a man pockets it.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: One who receives or agrees to something offered is a recipient, a man who takes.

clue.text: She is not the pick of the bunch

definitions.text: She is not the pick of the bunch

parts.words: She is not the pick of the bunch
parts.note: a shy girl left unasked at a dance, punning on a garden flower growing against brickwork

explanation.definitionFit: A shy woman left sitting out at a dance is never chosen, and the name is also a garden plant.

clue.text: Fine candlestick

definitions.meaning: a penalty, specifically an old Oxford college forfeit imposed at dinner
a bracket holding a candle fixed to a wall

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an Oxford dining-hall forfeit, a penalty, and a wall bracket for a candle.

clue.text: In the unlikely event of an opportunity to get away

definitions.text: In the unlikely event of an opportunity to get away

parts.words: In the unlikely event of an opportunity to get away
parts.note: a phrase for acting in slim hope

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means acting in faint hope of something happening, and literally a chance of getting off.

clue.text: The shape for a floor-covering

parts.note: a mat is a small floor-covering

explanation.surface: A rug's outline is being described.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the layout or arrangement of something is its overall shape.

clue.text: See 7
Some jazz in Chicago is elementary!

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Playing a little jazz in Chicago is easy stuff, the clue exclaims.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc is a chemical element, so it 'is elementary' in the sense of being one of the elements.

clue.text: Bound to have guidance verging on indecency

parts.note: a bound is a boundary or border
a line is a direction or policy to follow, as in a party line

explanation.surface: Someone obliged to give advice that is nearly indecent.
explanation.definitionFit: Material close to the boundary of acceptability is described as marginal or nearly over the line.

clue.text: Make a mistake in the blue reef

indicators.note: in means one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: sky blue, and the sky is often called the blue
to make a mistake is to err

explanation.surface: A sailor errs and runs onto a reef in the blue sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' for SKY is the old idiom 'out of the blue', the sky; the surface wants it to be the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish word for a rocky islet or reef in the sea.

clue.text: The first campanologist could he be a troublemaker?

definitions.text: The first campanologist could he be a troublemaker?

parts.words: The first campanologist could he be a troublemaker?
parts.note: the head bell-ringer of a team literally leads the ringing, while the phrase means an instigator of trouble

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the instigator of a riot or plot, and literally the head of a bell-ringing team.

clue.text: Latin translation Leslie had in the islands

indicators.note: a translation turns the word into another form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: Les is the short form of the name Leslie

explanation.surface: Leslie produced a Latin translation while in the Caribbean islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' rearranges LATIN into ANTIL; then LES, short for Leslie.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean archipelago, Greater and Lesser, is a chain of islands.

clue.text: Dingy drinking-place near -Edinburgh

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown, so dingy
a bar is a place for drinking

explanation.surface: A grimy pub on the outskirts of the Scottish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: DUNBAR is a coastal town in East Lothian, about 30 miles east of Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: The town lies on the coast east of the Scottish capital, so it is a place close to it.

clue.text: Roughly its dimensions are more or less correct

parts.note: about means roughly, approximately
a thing's dimensions are its measurements

explanation.surface: A measurement estimated roughly turns out to be nearly right.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, as in 'that's ... ', agrees that a summary is broadly accurate.

clue.text: Father has wrinkles

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
to have something is to own it

explanation.surface: Dad is getting lines on his face.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to frown is to wrinkle the brow, so he wrinkles.

clue.text: See 16
Most uneven?

parts.note: uneven read as not divisible by two, or as strangest of all

explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of a word meaning both strange and not divisible by two, so most irregular or most unpaired.

clue.text: But is it a co-ordinated system of transport in America?

definitions.text: But is it a co-ordinated system of transport in America?

parts.words: But is it a co-ordinated system of transport in America?
parts.note: the American word for a train network, which also means to rush something through without proper thought, hence the doubt about co-ordination

explanation.definitionFit: The US name for a railway also means to force something through hastily, hence the doubting question.

clue.text: Drink pop that is in Syria

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Drink pop that is in Syria' has no anagram indicator for POP to become PPO after ALE; similar clues read 'Drink fizzy pop', so a word seems lost.
annotationWithheld.clue: Drink pop that is in Syria

clue.text: Crazy about nothing suffering cold

indicators.note: about here means the jumbled letters go around the zero
suffering suggests being knocked about and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of this word are the fodder
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone driven crazy by nothing more than a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges CRAZY into CRYZA; 'about' puts it around O.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term for a head cold or nasal catarrh.

clue.text: Ship's tailor?

definitions.meaning: a small single-masted sailing vessel or a ship's boat
one who cuts cloth in a tailor's shop

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a small sailing vessel and also the tailor who cuts out garments.

clue.text: Leave fellows the Yorkshire section

parts.note: to leave is to depart
fellows are men
in Yorkshire dialect 'the' is shortened to t'

explanation.surface: Some men quit a Yorkshire part of an organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire speech famously clips 'the' to t', as in 'on t' moor'.
explanation.definitionFit: A division of an organisation or store is one section of it.

clue.text: Bird's speed over water

definitions.meaning: a wading shorebird of the sandpiper family
a nautical mile per hour, the unit of a ship's speed

explanation.definitionFit: The name of a sandpiper-like wader, and the nautical unit of one sea mile per hour.

clue.text: Make another part for an old thespian

indicators.note: part says only a portion of these words is taken, the run across them

explanation.surface: A request to write a new role for an aging actor.
explanation.walkthrough: EDMUND KEAN was a famous English tragic actor of the early 1800s.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Kean was a celebrated Regency stage actor, so a historic actor.

clue.text: Talk at endless rate before church

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the next
without an end means the final letter of the rate word goes

parts.note: speed is a rate of movement

explanation.surface: A preacher talking at a relentless pace in front of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the D of SPEED to leave SPEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a formal address or spoken words are a speech.

clue.text: Relating to the subject of the act I'm rewriting

indicators.note: rewriting means these letters are put together again in a new order

explanation.surface: A playwright reworking an act to suit its subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Concerned with a theme, the topic or subject matter of a work.
